title: Unlink a node_modules junction before deleting the tree that holds it
body: Unlink the junction first (fs.unlink on the link path, which Node reports as a symbolic link), then delete the tree. Never run git worktree remove --force on a worktree whose node_modules is a junction to the main checkout. If the main node_modules was emptied anyway, restore it with npm ci. Why: on 2026-10-07 git worktree remove --force followed the node_modules junction and emptied the main checkout's node_modules (0 entries left); fs.unlink on the junction followed by fs.rm recursive on the parent kept the target intact in a scratch test, and src/eval/agent/run.js unlinks its junction before removing each clone.
not_derivable: A Windows junction followed by git worktree remove --force empties the target; no code comment can show it before it happens.

evidence.summary: Unlinks the shared node_modules junction before removing the clone, naming git worktree remove --force as the reason.
